clues.text: This city stands in the far north of Russia. It lies east of the Yenisey River, south of the Taymyr Peninsula.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside the far north of Russia by the Yenisey River

source.quote: located south of the western Taymyr Peninsula, around 90 km (56 mi) east of the Yenisey River and 1,500 km (930 mi) north of Krasnoyarsk

clues.text: This city sits in a zone of permafrost, where the ground stays frozen and cold all year. It is one of just two large cities on such ground.
clues.narrowing: narrows to the few large cities built on ground that stays frozen all year

source.quote: Norilsk and Yakutsk are the only large cities in the continuous permafrost zone.

clues.text: Soviet leaders said yes to its big plant in nineteen thirty-five, and it was done by nineteen thirty-nine. Then the mines grew fast.
clues.narrowing: shortlists Soviet plant towns approved in 1935 and finished by 1939

source.quote: large-scale industrial mining only began after the Soviet Council of People's Commissars approved the construction of Norilsk Plant in 1935, which was completed by 1939.

clues.text: This city sits right on top of some of the largest nickel deposits on Earth. Digging and melting that ore is its main work.
clues.narrowing: near-decisive: the city built on some of Earth's largest nickel deposits

source.quote: Norilsk is located atop some of the largest nickel deposits on Earth. Consequently, mining and smelting ore are the major industries.

clues.text: No city in the world this far north holds so many people. It sits inside the Arctic Circle, in the far north.
clues.narrowing: converts: the northernmost large city in the world, inside the Arctic Circle

source.quote: It is the world's northernmost city with more than 175,000 inhabitants, and the second-largest city (after Murmansk) inside the Arctic Circle.
